'''''Hedychium coronarium''''', the '''white garland-lily'''<ref name=PLANTS>{{PLANTS | symbol = HECO11 | taxon = Hedychium coronarium | accessdate = 6 January 2017}}</ref> or '''white ginger lily''',<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN}}</ref> is a [[perennial]] flowering plant in the ginger family, [[Zingiberaceae]]. It is [[native species|native]] to the forest [[understorey]] of Asia.

Other common names include '''butterfly lily, Khumpui, fragrant garland flower, Indian garland flower, white butterfly ginger lily''', and '''white ginger'''.<ref name = RHSPF/>

==Description==
It is an upright perennial which may reach {{cvt|1-3|m|ft|abbr=on}} in height. It has long pointed leaves, with heavily scented white flowers with yellow bases.<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/8418/hedychium-coronarium/details | title = Hedychium coronaria | publisher = RHS | access-date = 7 September 2021}}</ref> In its native environment flowering occurs between August and December.<ref name=CABI>{{Cite web | url = http://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/26678|title=Hedychium coronarium (white butterfly ginger lily)|website=www.cabi.org|access-date=2017-02-15}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It is native to the [[Eastern Himalayan broadleaf forests|Eastern Himalayas]] of [[India]] ([[Sikkim]] and [[Tripura]]), [[Bangladesh]], [[Nepal]] and [[Bhutan]], through northernmost [[Myanmar]] and [[Thailand]], southern [[China]] ([[Yunnan]], [[Sichuan]], [[Hunan]], [[Guangxi]] and [[Guangdong]]) to [[Taiwan]] in the East.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200028392|title=Hedychium coronarium in Flora of China @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org|access-date=2017-02-15}}</ref><ref name=GRIN/>

It is typically found growing in forests.<ref name=":0" />

== As an invasive species ==
Beyond its native range, ''H. coronarium'' may be [[Invasive species|invasive]] in shallow water systems, along streams and in waterlogged areas. Once established, it is difficult to control due to vegetative reproduction through the underground spread of rhizomes.<ref name=":1" /> It was introduced in [[Brazil]] in the era of slavery, said to have been brought to the country by African slaves who used its leaves as mattresses, and is now considered naturalised in the states of [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]] (where it is classed as invasive), [[Bahia]] and [[Espírito Santo]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2007-01-01 |title=Floral biology of Hedychium coronarium Koen. (Zingiberaceae). |url=http://www.cabi.org/isc/abstract/20073239070 |journal=Revista Brasileira de Horticultura Ornamental |issn=1414-039X |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210918130406/https://www.cabi.org/isc/abstract/20073239070 |archive-date=2021-09-18 |access-date=2017-02-15}}</ref> This species was first introduced as an ornamental to [[Hawaii]] around 1888 by Chinese immigrants, and is now considered a serious invader in mesic to wet areas of [[Maui]] and [[Hawaii (island)|Hawaii island]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1998-01-01 |title=Impact of Alien Plants on Hawaiʻi's Native Biota. |url=http://www.cabi.org/isc/abstract/20097200324 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210918130400/https://www.cabi.org/isc/abstract/20097200324 |archive-date=2021-09-18 |access-date=2017-02-15}}</ref> Additionally, it is invasive in [[South Africa]], where it is a declared weed, and propagation of plant material is considered prohibited.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2008-01-01 |title=Ornamental plants as Invasive Aliens: Problems and Solutions in Kruger National Park, South Africa |url=http://www.cabi.org/isc/abstract/20067203829 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220330035306/https://www.cabi.org/isc/abstract/20067203829 |archive-date=2022-03-30 |access-date=2017-02-15}}</ref> It is also invasive in [[New Caledonia]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hequet |first=Vanessa |url=http://horizon.documentation.ird.fr/exl-doc/pleins_textes/divers12-08/010052239.pdf |title=Les espèces exotiques envahissantes de Nouvelle-Calédonie |year=2009 |page=17 |language=fr}}</ref>

== Cultivation ==
It is cultivated in warm [[Temperate climate|temperate]] and [[Subtropics|subtropical]] regions of the world as an ornamental. In China it is cultivated for use in medicine and production of [[Fragrance oil|aromatic oil]], due to the strong characteristic fragrance of the flowers, said to be reminiscent of [[jasmine]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/26678|title=Hedychium coronarium (white butterfly ginger lily)|website=www.cabi.org|access-date=2017-02-15}}</ref>

In the UK, it has received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF/>

===Hardiness===
It is [[evergreen]] in warmer climates, but deciduous in mild winter temperate regions of North America and Europe.<ref name=":1" /> In the UK it is rated by the Royal Horticultural Society as hardy down to {{cvt|-5|C|F|abbr=on}} in mild or coastal areas (H3).<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/rhs-hardiness-rating.pdf | title = Hardiness Ratings | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 18 September 2021}}</ref> 

===India===
It is also grown in state [[Tripura]], the Northeastern region of [[India]] and is known as ''Khumpui''. ''Hedychium coronarium'' is regarded sacred and is mentioned in folk tales of the [[Tripuri people]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=RSF-EEE Newsletter |url=https://www.iitg.ac.in/eee_rsf/Newsletter/Newsletter4/11_2.html |access-date=2024-12-28 |website=www.iitg.ac.in}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Living River to Commodified Island: The Tale of Dumboor... {{!}} NE Water Talk |url=https://newatertalk.in/blog/living-river-to-commodified-island-the-tale-of-dumboor |access-date=2024-12-28 |website=newatertalk.in}}</ref>

===Cuba===
''Hedychium coronarium'' is the [[National symbols of Cuba|national flower]] of Cuba, where it is known as ''mariposa'' (literally "butterfly") due to its shape. Women used to adorn themselves with these fragrant flowers in Spanish colonial times; because of the intricate structure of the inflorescence, women hid and carried secret messages important to the independence cause under it.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cubadiplomatica.cu/uganda/EN/LearnaboutCuba/Nativesymbols/NationalFlower.aspx|title=National Flower|publisher=Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Cuba|access-date=6 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140413144412/http://www.cubadiplomatica.cu/uganda/EN/LearnaboutCuba/Nativesymbols/NationalFlower.aspx|archive-date=13 April 2014}}</ref> The plant has become [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] in the cool rainy mountains in [[Sierra del Rosario]], Pinar del Rio Province in the west, the [[Escambray Mountains]] in the center of the island, and in the [[Sierra Maestra]] in the very east of it.

==Uses==
The flower buds and young flowers are edible.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-10-13 |title=Hedychium coronarium - White Ginger, White Garland-lily, Butterfly Ginger |url=https://wildlifeofhawaii.com/flowers/409/hedychium-coronarium-white-ginger/ |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=Hawaiian Plants and Tropical Flowers |language=en-US}}</ref>
